calibration.note: D-24: derived from exactly the D-17 calibration pair (n=2), which is not a calibration set. The two runs also differ in duration (3600s clean vs 900s contaminated), and max is duration-sensitive, so the clean arm's own 8.7 tail excursion ratio is a lower bound on what a clean 4 hour headline run might show; its 76.9% thread-max spread is also computed over very small values (18 to 78 us) where relative spread is naturally noisy. tail_excursion_ratio_max=50.0 and thread_max_spread_min=0.2 sit with wide margin on both sides of the two observed points (8.7/428.4 and 76.9%/3.6%) rather than hugging them, but they are not calibrated: do not read a Clean or Contaminated verdict produced under this status as a validated pass or fail. A provisional verdict is recorded on every run and rendered in REPORT.md, but it no longer decides admission to the headline series (D-28): admission is decided by determine_admission in crates/cli/src/cmd/run.rs from evidence causally upstream of the measured latency only, and never from this verdict or the tail metrics behind it. The per_run_hour interference-counter thresholds below remain unset, but the reason recorded here until 2026-09-04 was wrong: it said the contaminated run showed FEWER CAL/TLB/RES/device-IRQ counts than the clean run. Summing each arm's recorded per-CPU deltas over the isolated cores and normalising by duration gives, per run hour, CAL 6 clean vs 48 contaminated, TLB 6 vs 24, RES 55 vs 96, device IRQ 1127 vs 844. Only device IRQs invert, and CAL is higher even before normalising; the earlier reading compared raw totals across a 3600s/900s duration difference. The thresholds stay unset for a better reason: the magnitudes are implausible (one to two CAL IPIs per isolated CPU per hour, against roughly 137,000 on the contaminated 2026-08-28 baseline), so whatever these snapshots count is not the interference D-15 assumed, and two runs of unequal duration are not a calibration set. Plan 01-11 task 3 update (2026-09-04): 'calibrated' status per the plan's literal acceptance criteria was found unreachable, for the same reason the per_run_hour thresholds above are null, and status is kept 'provisional' rather than manufactured; see 01-11-SUMMARY.md deviations for the full account. derived_from intentionally still names only the original two runs: 2026-09-03-precision3591-calibration-contaminated (3600s, duration-matched to the 2026-09-01 clean arm, captured 2026-09-03 to address the duration mismatch noted above) is a later confirmatory run, not a source of these numbers, and under these same shipped thresholds it independently scores Contaminated (tail_excursion_ratio 211.2, thread_max_spread 3.7%), reinforcing rather than replacing this calibration. It is not added to derived_from because Thresholds::Provisional's own contract (crates/capture/src/interference.rs) and its rendered report text (crates/metrics/src/report.rs) both describe this status as derived from exactly the D-17 pair; see crates/capture/tests/interference.rs's calibration_pair_separates test, which exercises the original pair this file names.
